label: Data consent toggle
summary: The data consent toggle is a setting in ChatGPT that, when switched on, allows OpenAI to use your conversations as training data for their models. It is also a prerequisite for accessing both chat history and the browse feature, meaning users cannot use those features without consenting to data collection. Maaike treats it as a concrete example of how feature access and data extraction are bundled together.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses the data consent toggle as a case study in how AI products obscure the cost of new features. Her angle is sceptical: what looks like a useful browsing tool turns out to be primarily a mechanism for collecting more training data, and the toggle is the lever that makes that trade-off visible. She notes she was not aware of this coupling until she stumbled on it herself, and she frames that discovery as worth flagging to her audience.
open_questions: Is the browse experience within ChatGPT good enough to justify turning on the data toggle at all, given Maaike's note that it was subpar at the time?
Will OpenAI continue to gate useful features behind data consent as the product evolves?
